summary: The feature-chain spec and diagram agree with skills/feature-chain.md and skills/tdd.md on phases, order, gates and merge authority; nothing is contradicted or unsupported. Eight claims are true but rest on files outside the spec's sources (skills/co-plan.md, skills/to-prd.md, skills/code-refiner.md, skills/design-review.md, docs/agents-detail.md). The main omissions are the no-pause-between-phases rule, the architectural contribution mode, and the design feedback loop being absent from the spec.

code.overview: The chain itself is prose: skills/feature-chain.md tells the agent which skill to run next, and no script detects the entry point, writes design.md, prd.md or plan.md, or moves between phases. Code appears in three places: scripts/queue-model.ts carries a queued task's "chain" mode and architecture mode into the worker prompt, the commit hook and scripts/check-quality-mechanical.sh gate the commits and the refine step, and the queue delivery code plus CI and scripts/check-handoff.ts guard the final review and merge.

refs.anchor: 'model-led': 'Own architectural investigation, decisions and checks; the builder focuses on UX and product intent. Resolve technical design without requiring the builder to act as architect.',
refs.title: Architecture modes and the guidance text for each
refs.explain: Defines the three modes: builder-led, collaborative and model-led, with collaborative as the default. parseArchitecture throws on any other value. architectureGuidance returns the sentence for the mode and appends that validation, security and compatibility checks stay mandatory and release authority is unchanged.
refs.why: skills/feature-chain.md names this file as the source for how much of the technical design the agent owns versus asks the builder. It keeps the mode from being read as permission to skip checks or to merge.

refs.anchor: t.mode === 'chain' ? 'mode: chain (design→prd→plan→tdd→refine, autonomous, no questions)' : 'mode: direct',
refs.title: taskBlock: the prompt block a queue worker receives
refs.explain: Builds the text a worker gets for one task. The first line says "mode: chain" with the phase order, or "mode: direct". It then adds the architecture mode and its guidance, the docs/<slug>/ folder, the acceptance text, files, contracts and validate command when set, and wraps it all in a queue_task tag.
refs.why: This is how a queued task starts the chain and tells the worker which docs/<slug>/ folder to look in for existing artifacts. The worker still has to follow the skill text; this code only delivers the instruction.

refs.anchor: echo "pre-commit: tsconfig.json present but tsc not installed — skipping (install deps, e.g. npm ci)" >&2
refs.title: pre-commit hook: mechanical check, typecheck, skill routing gate
refs.explain: Runs on every git commit once core.hooksPath points at .githooks. It runs the mechanical quality check on the staged files, then tsc --noEmit if a tsconfig.json exists, then check-resolvable.ts and the skills-doc freshness check. The script runs under set -eu, so the first failing step aborts the commit.
refs.why: The TDD phase commits per slice, and the refiner fixes are committed after it. With the hook enabled each of those commits must pass the mechanical check and the typecheck; nothing checks the red/green order or tdd-log.md.

refs.anchor: "test:checks": "node scripts/check-resolvable.ts --strict && node scripts/update-skills-doc.ts --check && node scripts/check-agents-detail.ts && node scripts/check-handoff.ts && node scripts/check-guidelines.ts && node scripts/render-explorer-pages.ts --check && node scripts/render-diagrams.ts --check",
refs.title: package.json: what "the full suite" runs
refs.explain: npm test chains four scripts. test:node runs every *.test.ts under scripts/, tools/ and lib/ with node --test. test:tools runs each tool's own test file, test:shell runs every scripts/test-*.sh, and test:checks runs the repo checks. test:integration is separate and is not part of npm test.
refs.why: Refine starts only "when the full test suite passes". These scripts define that suite for this repo.

refs.anchor: emit "${file}:${MAX_LINES} [Readability/major] file is ${count} lines — exceeds ${MAX_LINES}-line limit; split into cohesive modules (or add a 'quality-ok: file-length — <reason>' pragma if it is one cohesive unit)"
refs.title: check_file: the 500-line file length check
refs.explain: Counts the lines in the file with wc -l. If the count is over MAX_LINES (500) and the file has no "quality-ok: file-length" pragma, it emits a Readability/major violation with the file name. Each emit adds one to VIOLATIONS, which makes the script exit non-zero at the end.
refs.why: /code-refiner must end with every rubric score at 10/10, and mechanical violations cannot be overridden. This is one of the three rubric rules a script decides rather than the reviewer agents.

refs.title: Quality Gate workflow: mechanical checks on all tracked source
refs.explain: On every pull request the job lists all tracked js, mjs, ts, tsx, sh, py, rb and go files with git ls-files. It passes the whole list to check-quality-mechanical.sh. Any violation makes the script exit 1, which fails the job.
refs.why: Re-runs the mechanical rubric rules on the PR. If the refiner pass left a mechanical violation, this job fails even though the agents reported 10/10.

refs.anchor: has skills/feature-chain.md 'QA'                "feature-chain Phase 4 summary reports QA"
refs.title: test-qa-skill.sh: feature-chain must run /qa and report it
refs.explain: Greps skills/qa.md for the "QA found" summary line. Then it greps skills/feature-chain.md for "/qa" and for "QA". finish prints the totals and returns non-zero if any assertion failed.
refs.why: The QA phase is done by the agent driving the real app. This test only keeps the chain wired to /qa and the QA line in the final summary; without it an edit could drop the step unnoticed.

refs.title: CI job "verify": npm test on every PR to main
refs.explain: On a pull request to main the job checks out the code, installs the Node version named in .node-version, runs npm ci, and then runs npm test. A failing test fails the job.
refs.why: When the agent has merge authority it must validate the PR first. This job is the hosted run of the full suite on that PR.

refs.title: selectDelivery and deliveryAllows: one task per delivery cycle
refs.explain: selectDelivery records a task id as the current delivery task, unless the queue is in batch mode or one is already recorded. deliveryAllows then answers whether a task may be claimed: always in batch mode, otherwise only when no task is selected or the task is the selected one.
refs.why: For a queued chain task the review phase "gates the next independent task" until its PR cycle ends. This is that gate: other tasks are not eligible while one delivery is open.

refs.anchor: console.log(`queue: DELIVERY PENDING — ${q.config.deliveryTask}; finish its PR/merge cycle and fresh branch, then advance`);
refs.title: Dispatch guard: DELIVERY PENDING
refs.explain: Before dispatching, if the queue is not in batch mode, a delivery task is recorded and nothing else is actionable, it prints DELIVERY PENDING with the task id and returns the DELIVERY exit code. Otherwise it returns with no block.
refs.why: A finished chain task without merge authority leaves its PR waiting for the owner. This message is what a drain loop sees instead of the next task.

refs.anchor: console.error('advance: requires selected completed task, no active claims, --pr <merged-pr-url> and --branch <fresh-working-branch>');
refs.title: queue advance: close the delivery cycle after the merge
refs.explain: cmdAdvance refuses unless the id is the selected delivery task, that task is done and accepted, no task is active, --pr looks like a pull request URL and --branch is not empty. On success it clears deliveryTask and deliveryAccepted, saves the queue and logs the PR and the fresh branch. Its own comment says it records what the root vouches for and does not check the remote.
refs.why: The chain ends with "confirm the merge and cut a fresh branch before the next task". This command is the only way to reopen dispatch, and it makes the orchestrator name the merged PR and the new branch.

refs.anchor: return existsSync(path) ? [`handoffs live only on branches; clear it before merging to main: git rm ${path} && git commit -m "chore: clear handoff before merge"`] : [];
refs.title: check-handoff.ts --pre-merge: no handoff file on the head to merge
refs.explain: preMerge returns an error when .pause/handoff.md still exists, with the git rm command that clears it. The CLI block below it picks preMerge when --pre-merge is passed, prints each error, and exits 1 if there is one.
refs.why: A merge to main must not carry a session handoff file. The orchestrator runs this on the head it merges; without it a later /resume on main could act on a stale handoff.

promptOnly.what: The agent runs /to-prd: it reads design.md and the codebase, confirms with the owner which modules need tests, writes prd.md and commits it, with no script involved.
